title: K4 letters as word counts through the K1-K3 plaintexts and the Morse text: walk (W), moving window (B) and letter pairs (C) over 56 word lists
k4_result: Rules W and B: 10,891,184 settings, each giving one full 97-letter reading. Best 10 of 24 clue letters (rule B, K1-K3 as carved with X dropped and LAYER TWO, third letter of the word, KRYPTOS numbering counted backwards, advance -22, start 53); 24 needed. By rule and mode: W ring 9, W line 7, W with no extra advance 8; B ring 10, B line 7, B with no extra advance 8. Mean per setting 1.43 of 24 for both rules. Settings with 9+: 24 (W 8, B 16); with 10+: 1; with 11+: 0. Readings are gibberish: the most English-looking of the 24 scores -6.49 per quadgram on the big model (English needs -5.1, noise is about -6.5), word coverage 0.08-0.13. Rule C with overlapping pairs: 53,484,800 settings, best 6/24 with strict letter numbers and 10/24 with letter numbers wrapping round the word, mean 0.95; readings -6.40 and -7.02. Rule C read strictly can reach at most 13 of the 24 clue letters on any list (5-13). Halved (non-overlapping) rule C: 876,800 readings of 48 letters hold BERLIN 0 times, CLOCK 0, NORTH 0, EAST 817.
controls: 20 shuffled K4s, same search. W and B: best 9-11 (ten at 9, eight at 10, two at 11); K4's 10 is equalled or beaten by 10 of 20. Per mode, shuffles at or above K4: W ring 20/20, W line 15/20, W plain 18/20, B ring 6/20, B line 19/20, B plain 10/20. Settings with 9+: 10-45 each (K4 24). Rule C: strict 5-6 (K4 6), wrapping 10-11 (K4 10); halved readings: BERLIN 0 in 19 shuffles and 4 in one, CLOCK 0, NORTH 0-108, EAST 648-1303 (K4 817). K4 sits inside the controls on every count.
planted: 6/6 (walk on first letters, plain A=1..Z=26 on a ring; walk on last letters, KRYPTOS numbering, ring; window moving 7 words a letter on first letters; window on a line on third letters counted backwards; walk on a line through K3; overlapping pairs with wrapping letter number). Each gave 24/24 at the planted list, letter, numbering, advance and start and was read back in full. The messages are strings of English words drawn so that every next letter is reachable, because ordinary English prose cannot be encoded (see scope).
scope_limits: Texts: only the K1, K2, K3 plaintexts and the Morse text as divided into words in kryptos/idea106_words.py (checked letter for letter against data/sculpture), alone and joined in order (K1-K2, K2-K3, K1-K3, K1-K3 then Morse, Morse then K1-K3); spelling as carved or corrected; X and K3's closing Q as words or dropped; K2 ending ID BY ROWS or X LAYER TWO: 56 word lists, 175 distinct lines of letters. Letter taken: number 1, 2, 3, 4 or the last of the word. Count: place of the K4 letter in A-Z or KRYPTOS order, forwards or backwards, plus a fixed advance of -30..30 words per letter (this holds numbering from 0 or 1 and the text read backwards), every start word, ring and line. Rule C only as overlapping neighbour pairs (letter number from A-Z or KRYPTOS place, from 0 or 1, from the front or the end of the word, strict or wrapping) and, halved, as a search for the clue words with no advance. NOT covered: a count that also depends on a key word; a different word division (EARTHS, WW, the Morse fragments T IS, RQ, e-padding); letters counted from the end other than the last; a rule that changes which letter is taken from word to word; nulls; a transposition before or after; counts over 26; texts not on the sculpture; words of the cipher panel. Pre-filter: the window rule passes (matches in place, K5 words encrypt alike) but only with a crutch: 33% of English letters have no word in their window and were written as themselves, so the card's marks are not reliable; the walk has state and would be FLAGGED for K5 as in idea 85. Separate finding, not a search limit: on K1-K3 ordinary English cannot be encoded at all by W or B (0 of 200 messages of 97 letters for every letter position and advance; a walk dies after a median of 3-6 letters, longest 41), and by overlapping pairs 1 of 200. First letters hold no J, V, Z and only 7 E in 163 words; last letters hold no B, J, K, L, P, V, Z.

negative.family: Cipher letter as a word count through the solved K1-K3 text (prisoner letter code / book-style reading)
negative.hypothesis: Each K4 letter is a number of words to count through the K1-K3 plaintext (or the Morse text), and one fixed letter of the word reached (first, second, third, fourth or last) is the plaintext; as a running walk, as a window that moves a fixed number of words per letter, or with a neighbouring K4 letter giving the letter number.
negative.scope: P_i = letter k of word s + a*i +- d(C_i) (window) or of word s + a*i +- (d(C_0)+..+d(C_i)) (walk); 56 word lists (K1, K2, K3, joins in order, Morse; carved/corrected spelling, X kept/dropped, both K2 endings); k = 1-4 or last; d in A-Z or KRYPTOS order, both directions; a = -30..30; every start; ring and line: 10,891,184 settings. Overlapping pairs (word from C_i, letter number from C_(i+-1), 16 letter numberings): 53,484,800 settings. Halved pairs: 876,800 readings searched for the clue words.
negative.outcome: Dead: best 10/24 clue letters where 24 are needed (walk 9, window 10, pairs 10), readings gibberish at -6.5 on the big model (controls: 20 shuffled K4s give 9-11 and 10-11; planted 6/6 found at 24/24 and read back). Also: ordinary English cannot be encoded by counting words through K1-K3 with a fixed letter position (0 of 200 messages by walk or window, a walk dies after 3-6 letters), so the method is unworkable on this text however it is set.

follow_ups: Acrostic the other way round: instead of K4 pointing into K1-K3, test whether K1-K3 was WRITTEN to carry a message (first/last/n-th letters of its words read at a fixed interval, as the wartime letter codes did). The first-letter line BSSATAOLLTNOI... is 163 letters; a short skip-read of it for English is a one-minute test and needs no K4.

Word counting fails because one fixed letter position is too poor (7 words in 163 start with E). The only way it can carry English is if the K4 letter also chooses the letter inside the word without a second cipher letter, e.g. value = word count mod m and letter number = value div m. A two-digit split of 0..25 (m = 2..13) is a small exact test.
